skill.name: zapier-workflows
skill.description: Use Zapier MCP tools and user-owned webhooks to document, trigger, and maintain reusable automation workflows from Claude Code.
skill.summary: Document and run Zapier MCP and webhook workflows from AI coding tools.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static command and URL detections are documentation false positives, but the skill has real risk from plaintext webhook secrets and hidden persistent skill storage. It also instructs external Zapier workflow execution through Bash and durable self-editing, so publication should require clear warnings and safer defaults.

remediation.issue: Plaintext webhook URLs are stored in skill reference files.
remediation.suggestion: Store webhook URLs in a secret manager or environment-specific config, and keep only symbolic workflow names in the skill files.

remediation.issue: Webhook execution can cause external side effects without a required confirmation gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before any Zap sends messages, changes records, spends money, or calls third-party services.

remediation.issue: Self-editing reference files can persist sensitive or unsafe instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before saving new patterns, redact sensitive values, and provide a review command for all saved changes.

remediation.issue: The setup example includes a token-shaped bearer value.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the redacted token-shaped sample with a simple placeholder such as [your-token] everywhere.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Webhook Credential Storage
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users that webhook URLs contain authentication tokens and stores those URLs in editable skill reference files. Anyone who can read those files may trigger user Zaps.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly states webhook URLs contain authentication tokens and instructs the assistant to record them in skill references. This is direct evidence of plaintext credential storage risk.

semantic_findings.title: External Workflow Execution Without Explicit Confirmation Gate
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the assistant to trigger Zapier webhooks with Bash curl commands after matching a request. It does not require a confirmation step before workflows cause external side effects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The execution pattern and examples instruct Bash-based webhook POST requests and only mention confirming after execution. That creates clear external side-effect risk.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Self-Modifying Workflow Memory
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to edit its own reference files and persist user workflow details across sessions. Sensitive preferences or unsafe instructions could become durable behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The self-learning protocol directly instructs Read and Edit tool use to make durable changes. The behavior is intentional and documented, but it increases persistence and privacy risk.

content.user_title: Automate Zapier Workflows in Claude Code
content.value_statement: Zapier users often lose workflow context across AI sessions. This skill records preferred tools, webhook Zaps, and reusable patterns for Claude Code, Claude, and Codex.
actual_capabilities: Documents user-owned Zapier webhook workflows in a reusable reference file.
Guides Zapier MCP setup for Claude Code and related AI tools.
Reads saved workflow patterns before choosing MCP tools or webhook Zaps.
Triggers configured webhook Zaps with POST requests when the user asks.
Prompts users to save repeatable automation patterns after successful workflows.
limitations: It does not include real working Zaps in the template files.
It requires user-provided Zapier MCP tools, webhook URLs, or both.
Webhook URLs are sensitive and must not be committed to public repositories.
It cannot verify that an external Zap completed unless the workflow reports status.

use_cases.title: Run Team Automation
use_cases.description: Trigger documented Zaps for daily digests, lead alerts, or reporting workflows from a natural language request.

use_cases.title: Reuse Research Patterns
use_cases.description: Store preferred research tools, output destinations, and follow-up steps for repeatable market or technical research.

use_cases.title: Track Structured Data
use_cases.description: Use saved MCP patterns to add expenses, leads, or task records to the correct connected system.

prompt_templates.title: List My Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Check which Zapier MCP tools are available and tell me what workflows I can build with them.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Webhook Zap
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me document a new webhook-triggered Zap, including trigger phrases, expected output, timing, and safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Save a Workflow Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this successful workflow as a reusable pattern with the trigger words, tool sequence, parameters, and confirmation message.

prompt_templates.title: Audit My Automation Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my saved Zapier workflow references for outdated patterns, missing prerequisites, duplicate triggers, and sensitive data exposure.

output_examples.output: The skill checks the documented Zaps, triggers the matching webhook, and confirms the expected delivery channel and timing.

output_examples.input: Research new competitors and save the useful results.
output_examples.output: The skill reads the saved MCP pattern, uses the preferred research tool, summarizes results, and records them in the configured destination.

output_examples.input: Remember that expenses go to my Personal Budget sheet.
output_examples.output: The skill updates the saved tool preference so future expense tracking uses the named sheet.

best_practices: Store real webhook URLs outside public repositories and rotate exposed URLs immediately.
Require explicit confirmation before workflows send messages, spend money, or change records.
Review saved patterns regularly to remove stale tools, duplicate triggers, and sensitive details.
anti_patterns: Commit skill files that contain real Zapier webhook URLs or authorization tokens.
Treat placeholder examples as working Zapier credentials or production workflow definitions.
Save one-off or sensitive temporary requests as permanent automation patterns.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps AI tools document, choose, and run Zapier MCP actions and webhook-triggered Zaps.

faq.question: Does the template include real workflows?
faq.answer: No. The included reference files are templates that users replace with their own workflows.

faq.question: Do I need Zapier MCP?
faq.answer: No. The skill can use webhooks only, MCP tools only, or both together.

faq.question: Are webhook URLs sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Many webhook URLs act like credentials because anyone with the URL can trigger the Zap.

faq.question: Can the skill update its own reference files?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs Claude Code to update workflow references when the user teaches new patterns.

faq.question: Is this safe for public repositories?
faq.answer: Only if all real webhook URLs, tokens, tool preferences, and private workflow details are removed first.
